sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *cuando* + preterite and *mientras* from A2 Unit 13: *cuando* links an event to the moment another happened, and *mientras* links two things that go on at the same time. The Amazon, with its rubber boom and its river life, is full of "when" and "while". Here they work on Manaus and Belém.

sections.title: When and while on the river
rows: Cuando bajó el precio del caucho, la economía de la región entró en crisis.
*cuando* + preterite: an event, then its result
Mientras el caucho valía mucho, Manaus crecía.
*mientras* + imperfect: two things going on together
Los pasajeros descansan en hamacas mientras el barco avanza.
*mientras* + present: now, at the same time
Cuando llegaron los viajeros a Manaus, vieron el Encuentro de las Aguas.
*cuando* can also open the sentence for a sequence

items.spanish: Cuando se inauguró el Teatro Amazonas, Manaus vivía el auge del caucho.
items.english: When the Teatro Amazonas was inaugurated, Manaus was living the rubber boom.

items.spanish: Mientras la lluvia caía, el río subía.
items.english: While the rain fell, the river rose.

items.spanish: Se vende pescado en el mercado mientras la gente compra frutas.
items.english: Fish is sold at the market while people buy fruit.

sections.content: With *cuando* + preterite, one event follows or triggers another. With *mientras*, both actions continue together, so imperfect (past) or present (now) is normal. When *cuando* opens the sentence, put a comma after its clause.
